questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: seeing a core's own state and history
questions.question: The spec says a core's name and history show on "the core's own Part History page" (S5-E3), but no screen we know opens that page: the core has no row on the Inventory list, in Export or on the Part Library list. (a) How does a user open a core's own Part History page? (b) Does the global search in the top bar list a core ("Core for …"), with the grey Inactive tag and "Not Tracked" like any other part?
questions.options:
(a) A) From the part's own Part History page (please say where). B) From Parts → Returns ("Core for …" rows). C) There is no way on screen.
(b) A) Yes, cores are listed like other parts. B) No, cores are not listed.
sources: QA lead's answer of 9 Oct 2026, situation 5

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: a part with no bin location
questions.question: Turning tracking on for a part with no bin location gives it the location's default bin (S5-R7). In the part window the last bin can never be removed (Story 4 note), and the import puts a part with no bin into an "Unassigned" bin (S7-N10). How does a part end up with no bin location at all, so a tester can check S5-R7?
questions.options:
A) Delete its only bin location in Bin Locations while the part holds 0 there.
B) Save an untracked part with its bin row removed (the window allows it while tracking is off).
C) Only old data has such parts.
D) Another way (please say).
questions.v33_check: v33 unchanged on this point. Still open. S5-01 is written with route A and held until answered.

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: the Delete button in an open Edit Library Part window
questions.question: If the last part using a Part Library entry is deleted while the entry's "Edit Library Part" window is open in another tab, does that window's Delete button become enabled without a reload?
questions.options:
A) Yes, without a reload.
B) Only after the window is closed and opened again.
C) Only after the page is reloaded.
questions.v33_check: v33 unchanged (S11-R3c says nothing about refresh). Still open.
questions.integration_27oct: Still open (v33 S11-R3c says nothing about refresh). S12-06 (C425620) held on it.

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: parts added by the parts import
questions.question: (a) Is a part that the parts import adds tracked or untracked? (b) Is the import template's "name" column the part's description?
questions.options: (a) A) Always tracked. B) It depends on the file (please say which column). (b) A) Yes. B) No (please say which column).
sources: Tech plan Phase 6 (the import never writes is_tracked / is_active)
questions.v33_check: v33 S7-N10 still speaks of "an import row that adds a tracked part" without saying how a row is tracked. The tech plan says the import never writes the tracking flag (so a new part would take the default, tracked); the tech plan informs and never overrules, so this stays a question.
questions.integration_27oct: Phase B: S7-25 (C573682) is written and held on Q4(a). Q4(b) (is the template's name column the description?) is not held: S7-22, S7-23, S7-24 say 'the description cell', and the setup-file line (claude=) names the name column as the open question.

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: where Bin Locations is
questions.question: The spec says Bin Locations is under "Administration" (S5-E2), and the 14 Oct answer 5 says the same, but on screen it is under Settings. Which name should the tests use?
questions.options:

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: the close X on status confirmations
questions.question: The design draws a close X at the top right of every status confirmation (Deactivate part?, Activate part?, Deactivate parts?, Activate parts?). The PRD lists only a title, a message, an optional note, Cancel and a confirm button. (a) Should the X be there? (b) If yes, does clicking it do the same as Cancel (nothing changes, and from the part window the picked status is kept)?
questions.options:
A) Keep the X; it acts as Cancel.
B) No X: title, message, note, Cancel and the confirm button only.
sources: PRD v33 §4 Key Decisions: "Every confirmation is the application's standard dialog. A title, a message, an optional note, Cancel and a confirm button."
SV-10823 UI/UX: "Standard confirmation with title, message lines, optional note, Cancel and a red Deactivate or blue Activate button."

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: the note on design board 7.2
questions.question: The note on design board 7.2 still says a Part Library entry "can be edited and deleted" on its page, while the PRD (S11-R3) says the page itself has no Delete button and Delete sits in the Edit Library Part window. The board's picture shows no Delete. Can you confirm the PRD is right and the note is out of date? Our cases follow the PRD.
questions.options:
A) The PRD is right; the note is out of date.
B) The page should have a Delete button.
sources: Design board 7.2 note: "Clicking a row opens the entry, where it can be edited and deleted (S11-R3)."

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: long Part History entries
questions.question: When a Part History entry is long (for example a part number change ending "| Changed at: <location>"), the design (board 2.6) wraps it onto a second line inside the Event column. The engineering plan cuts the Event text off with "..." instead. Which is right: (a) wrap onto more lines, or (b) cut off with "..."? If (b), how does a user read the full entry?
questions.options:
A) Wrap onto more lines (as the design).
B) Cut off with "..." (as the tech plan).
sources: PRD v33 S10-R21 (silent on wrap or cut-off)
Design board 2.6 note: "Staff, Date and Time keep their production widths; a long Event wraps onto a second line."
Tech plan Phase 8, PartHistory.vue: "S10-R21: fixed headerStyle widths on Staff/Date/Time, Event elastic, table-layout: fixed + ellipsis (the Inventory list approach)"

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: who can open Parts → Returns and start a vendor return today
questions.question: The spec now says opening Parts → Returns and starting a vendor return "keep the access today's 'Vendor Order Management' settings give" (S9-N3a), without naming that access. So the tests compare the build with production. Please state today's access so the tests can say it directly: (a) Can a role with no Vendor Order Management permission open Parts → Returns? (b) Can a role with Vendor Order Management → View, but not Create & Edit, start a vendor return? (c) Which role, if any, reaches a return's or a vendor credit's part search without Part Library & Inventory → View, so the standard access error of S9-N3 can be seen? (Vendor Order Management → Create & Edit includes Part Library & Inventory → View, S9-N3a.)
questions.options:
(a) A) Yes. B) No.
(b) A) Yes. B) No, the button is hidden. C) No, it is greyed out.
(c) A) A role with Vendor Order Management → View only. B) No role on screen today (the error is reached only outside the screens).
sources: Jira SV-10822, Nemanja Djuric and Chris Ward, 23 Oct 2026
questions.note: Not held: S9-41 and S9-42 run today as a side-by-side comparison with production (S12-N1: every user's access on release day is identical to the day before). If the answer to (c) is B, S9-N3's access error is a NO MANUAL CASE.

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: renaming a part to a look-alike of another part at the same location
questions.question: A part's number is changed, in Edit Inventory Part, to one that matches another part at the SAME location once case and punctuation are ignored (for example AB-100 is stocked here and another part is renamed to ab 100). Story 7 says the save is refused with "AB-100 already exists at this location." (S7-N3, S7-N5b). The new S13-N1a refuses a rename that matches a part "at any location that stocks this part" with "AB-100 already exists at Staging Heavy Duty." ("{existing part number} already exists at {location}."). Which message shows when the look-alike is at this same location?
questions.options:
A) Story 7's: "AB-100 already exists at this location."
B) S13-N1a's: "AB-100 already exists at <this location's name>."

questions.topic: Part Library: when do the other Part Library refusals show?

We can test "This Part Library entry is in use and cannot be deleted." and "Part Library entry not found." on screen. For the others, which screen action shows them, if any: (a) "Part Library entry not found" (no full stop); (b) "Part Library entry not found for ID: {id}." and "... for part number: {part number}."; (c) "Part Library entry missing category." (a part request from an entry with no category); (d) "A part from the Part Library must have Vendor as its source."?
questions.options: For each: A) It shows on screen when you ... (please say how). B) Only from outside the screens (no manual test).

questions.topic: Part Library: where the special order's cost shows
questions.question: S12-R14b now says a special-order result from two vendors uses the most recent delivery's vendor AND cost. Our test reads the cost in the Cost field after the result is picked in New Part Request. Is that where the cost of the result shows?
questions.options:
A) Yes, the Cost field fills with that delivery's cost.
B) It shows somewhere else (please say where).

questions.topic: Part dialog: a renamed part on an open work order line
questions.question: After a part is renamed, what number does a line that already holds the part (picked onto an open work order) show? The spec keeps the line (S13-R18) and lists the open work that takes the new number (S13-R19: purchase order lines, part requests, canned jobs, returns), but not work order part lines; the tech plan leaves those lines unchanged.
questions.options:
A) The line keeps the old number.
B) The line shows the new number.
questions.note: No case asserts either answer now (the 14 Oct S13-20 line that expected the old number was removed: no PRD sentence supports it).

questions.topic: Part Lifecycle: a page opened before the user's role lost the Delete permission
questions.question: Three tests open a part page as user D while user D's role still has 'Part Library & Inventory → Delete', then an Admin takes that permission off the role in another window, then user D carries on in the page that was already open: a bulk status change and a delete (S8-N3), turning tracking off (S8-N2), and saving a new untracked part (S8-N1). The tests expect the open page to keep showing its old controls (Delete Part, Part Status, the tracking switch) until it is reloaded, and the save to be refused with the access denied error. Does a page that was loaded before a role change keep showing its old controls until the user reloads it?
questions.options:
A) Yes: the open page keeps its controls until it is reloaded, and the save is refused with the access denied error.
B) No: the open page updates at once and hides the controls, so the refusal can only be reached from outside the screens (the three tests become developers' checks).
sources: PRD v33 Story 8 context note ("The system checks that access itself, so hiding the controls is not the only protection.")
questions.note: Not held: no source says an open page changes when a role changes, so the tests are written for answer A. If the answer is B, S8-N1, S8-N2 and S8-N3 move to No manual case and these three tests are deleted or rewritten.
